the development of a multi-criteria decision support tool to help stakeholders reach a consensus about the performance indicators that are important to them in the context of marine protected area management.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MPA is a compromise, a trade-off between different interests and that the MPA management should be a continuous process.
no single group is more important than another, as all are equally relevant to the MPA.
no one stakeholder group has an overriding influence in decision-making in the MPA, and that all groups are equally influential in the decision-making process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multi-criteria analysis is an appropriate tool to identify the preferences of the different stakeholder groups.
the stakeholders are in agreement on what the MPA management should achieve, but they are not in agreement on how to achieve these goals.
the MPA is not yet a clear priority for the majority of stakeholders and that the management of the reserve is still in a formative phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the development of a hierarchy of performance indicators should not be a top-down process, as it has traditionally been in the past, but should be a participatory process, where the stakeholders themselves are involved in the process.

a multi-criteria decision approach can be useful to understand stakeholder positions in marine protected area management, and to identify the most important performance indicators to be used in MPA management.

there is a need to consider the different perspectives of the stakeholders in order to develop a management strategy that can accommodate all of them, and that a multi-criteria decision-making process is an effective tool in this respect.
